description: methods/mod.rs:377-380 — 'pub fn with_sort_ascending(mut self, v: bool) -> Self'. At call sites: 'input.with_sort_ascending(true)' or 'input.with_sort_ascending(false)' — the meaning of the bool is opaque without consulting the doc-string. The Rust review guide explicitly calls out this anti-pattern: 'bool parameters that are really two-variant enums in disguise. fn process(input: &str, verbose: bool) — the caller cannot tell at the call site what true means.' Idiomatic form: 'pub enum SortDirection { Ascending, Descending }' with 'with_sort_direction(SortDirection::Ascending)'. The underlying MessageQueryInput.sort_ascending field can stay as bool (since the wire serialization to 'isAscending: bool' matches), and the conversion happens in the setter. Counter-argument: this is purely call-site readability; sort_ascending is a near-universal builder convention name. The counter-argument has some weight — bool-for-sort-direction is widely tolerated. Marking as P4 + opinion because the engineering basis (call-site readability) is weak relative to the API churn cost (introducing a new enum + setter rename).
title: MessageQueryInput::with_sort_ascending(bool) is bool-as-enum at call sites
